original_question: Generalize domain wall boundary conditions from the six-vertex model to other integrable models in such a way that the partition function retains the key determinant property: it should be representable as a determinant whose dimension is proportional to the size of the system.
target_in_paper: Section V.4, 'Further Generalizations': the unnumbered open problem asking for analogues of domain wall boundary conditions for other models that preserve the determinant-partition-function feature of the six-vertex DWBC case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's core target very well: it identifies the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions as the source example, asks for a generalization to other models, and correctly singles out the key structural requirement that the partition function remain expressible as a determinant whose size scales proportionally with the system size. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))
missing_details: The paper ties the desired feature specifically to the six-vertex DWBC partition-function formula discussed in Section V, where DWBC are defined and Izergin's determinantal formula is recalled in equations (18)-(21); that benchmark should be made explicit in a stand-alone reformulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))

The scope in Section V.4 is 'other models,' not an unrestricted statement about all integrable models, so the refined question should avoid broadening the paper's target. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))

What must be generalized is the boundary condition itself: the paper asks for generalizations of domain wall boundary conditions, not merely for determinant formulas for already-fixed models. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))

The determinant is meant to have dimension proportional to the system size in the same structural sense as the six-vertex DWBC determinant, so the refined question should state that the determinant size is required to scale linearly with the finite lattice size parameter. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))

The nearby context notes already-known examples only as partial precedents, so the question should not redescribe those examples as the target problem; they serve only to delimit the intended neighborhood of the problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))

No ambient field/ring, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, operator-definition, or 'for all sufficiently large m' conditions occur here; this is a model-construction problem about partition functions and boundary conditions rather than an algebraic-geometry or polynomial-identity problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))
refined_question: For models beyond the six-vertex model, can one construct genuine generalizations of domain wall boundary conditions such that the corresponding partition function, in direct analogy with the six-vertex DWBC formula highlighted in Section V, admits a determinantal representation whose matrix dimension is proportional to the system size? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section V.4 rather than the neighboring open problem in Section V.3: Section V.3 concerns bulk and boundary correlation functions, whereas Section V.4 explicitly isolates as the 'main feature' of formula (19) that the six-vertex DWBC partition function is given by a determinant of system-size order, and then states the open problem of obtaining analogous DWBC generalizations for other models. The Section V opening discussion supplies the needed context by defining DWBC and recalling the determinantal partition-function formula before Section V.4 formulates the problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))
